The following is a transcript of an interview between Kelli Sander (KS) and Tanya Kuhn (TK) for The 504 Diaries, a digital history project of the 504 Sit-In by UC Berkeley's Department of Ethnic Studies (formerly the Ethnic Studies Library, formerly the Ethnic Studies Resource Center). It is one of several interviews that have been conducted by the 504 Diaries with participants of the 1977 sit-in. This interview is available online as an mp3 file here.
Kelli Sander: Can you introduce yourself for the record?
Kuhn: Sure, my name is Tanya Kuhn, and I am from Berkeley, California.
KS: Great. Can you tell us a little bit about the events of February and April 1977?
TK: Sure. Well, in February of 1977, I had a friend named Pat who needed a job, and we'd been working on getting her a job together, and she was in a lot of trouble. The government agency had denied her request for housing. It's a little complicated, but basically she was in the position of needing the housing but not having it, and then they were going to send her off, and she was a disabled person, so she was in a difficult position of being disabled. So I was helping her with a job, and I was going to go with her to the interview. But she had a job interview and a hearing on the same day, so I ended up going to the hearing with her. And they had the hearings at a place called the Federal Building, and when I walked in I saw that the Federal Building had stairs. And at that time I was not using a wheelchair or any kind of mobility aid, but I had difficulty walking and it wasn't obvious that I had a disability. But I noticed the stairs and I looked at this building, and I realized that I could not go up those stairs. And I realized, this is going to be a problem, because if they need me to see a doctor, or they need me to come here for any kind of a hearing or anything, how am I going to do that? And there was nothing accessible. And so I realized, okay, this is a problem.
